item.title: Christian persecution in Nigeria worrisome — Catholic bishops
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara Church leaders have expressed concern over the increasing cases of violent persecution of Christians in parts of Nigeria, saying the disturbing trend has worsened over the past two decades. The Apostolic Nuncio to Nigeria, Archbishop Michael Francis Crotty, and the Archbishop of Owerri, Most Rev. Lucius Iwejuru Ugorji, raised the concern at the weekend in Owerri during their respective addresses at the 18th National Conference of the Association of Papal Knights and Medalists in Nigeria (APKMN). In his address, Crotty said Christians had suffered persecution in different forms throughout Nigeria’s history, but noted that violent forms of persecution had become more pronounced in the last two decades. “In the history of Nigeria, Christians have suffered persecution in different forms, and this disturbing phenomenon has increased within the last two decades, especially the violent forms of persecution. “In recent years, Christians have been targeted by kidnappers, and many lay faithful and priests have been kidnapped. “Many of those kidnapped were killed, and others were released after ransoms were paid. Thousands of churches have been attacked and destroyed since the beginning of Boko Haram and the activities of herdsmen in more recent years,” he said. The Apostolic Nuncio also alleged that Christians in some parts of the country, particularly the North and North-Central regions, had been denied legitimate access to land for the construction of places of worship. “Very often the issue of persecution of Christians in Nigeria is politicised and approached with some sort of bias and religious sentiments. “There is no doubt that people of other faiths have also been affected by insecurity in Nigeria. However, we cannot deny the fact that Christians have been specifically targeted in some parts of the country. “Our concern should be the necessary actions to take in order to bring the unnecessary killing of all citizens to an end, whether they are Christian or of other faiths,” he said. He described the conference theme, “Strategic Engagements in Addressing Christian Persecution in Nigeria: Toward Coordinated Response”, as timely, stressing the need for collective action across religious and community lines. In his address, Archbishop Ugorji said the human and material consequences of the country’s insecurity remained alarming, irrespective of whether the crisis was viewed as targeted persecution of Christians or a complex socio-economic conflict. “Ultimately, whether the crisis is perceived as a targeted persecution of Christians or a complex socio-economic conflict, the human and material toll is undeniable. “It is deeply troubling that tens of thousands have lost their lives, millions remain internally displaced, the education of thousands of children is truncated, and millions of naira have been lost through destruction of property and paying ransom,” he said. item.title: Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu THE governor of Edo, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has said the state already has the structure for state police to commence and for that reason, the state House of Assembly was one of the first to pass the law as recommended by the National Assembly. Okpebholo spoke in an interview with journalists in Benin-City as part of activities to mark his second year anniversary. “We are prepared. We were one of the first to sign into law, when others were talking, we said no, it is working for us and right now, to be honest with you, even with our vigilantes, we already have state police because it is working for us. Edo state is safe.” He said his state already has a working security architecture it has tested that could be used to track criminals even outside the state,” he said. Okpebholo said “Remember there was this kidnapping that happened and within 24 hours which has never happened in Nigeria, we got the guys, so that is it. We are prepared to go to other states when they take any of our citizens. We did it in Kogi, then something happened in Ogun, I called the governor, I said, please, I don’t want my person to stay with this kidnapper for more than five days and as God would have it, he was able to get them out within a short time. So somebody has to be prudent with everything.” On security in the state, Governor Okpebholo said his administration took stiff measures to reduce the level of killings and kidnapping in the state. Some of the measures, he said, was destroying any building that was linked to kidnapping and cult related activities in the state irrespective of the social status of the person involved. He said: “These are stiff measures we have taken that are really working for us. To be honest with you, if not that we have done that, maybe you won’t be able to stay in Benin for two nights. Today nightlife is back, business is booming at night, even supermarkets are beginning to open at night. “In the next few weeks, it will be safer because there will be police at every corner of the state to watch everyone. They will be equipped even with motorbikes so that when somebody thinks he can run, then they will follow the person. Whether you take a bush path, they will follow you up.” The post Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Yari to critics: You did nothing about insecurity for 20 yrs
item.description: …Says, FAAC allocations now in trillions By Omeiza Ajayi The Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has told those saying the party has no plan for security that they did nothing about insecurity in 20 years. He spoke on Saturday at the APC presidential rally in Jos, the Plateau State capital. “Those who are saying we don’t have plan for security, I want to remind them that they did nothing about insecurity for over 20 years about it because it started during their time,” Yari said. According to him, the APC will implement its manifesto to the letter, promising that by 2031 almost everything promised would have been achieved. Yari told the gathering that Plateau’s political players had come out to assure the President of the state’s votes in the 2027 general election. “The key players, active players in the Plateau politics are all here before you to give you the assurances that 2027 Plateau is 101% assured,” he said. He described Tinubu as “the person that met the federation account of Nigeria as at June 2023 at N732 billion. But today, we thank God, Mr President, we thank you for your hard work and your special leadership. We are now counting the federation account in trillions.” The post Yari to critics: You did nothing about insecurity for 20 yrs appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu Northern Youth Forum dumps president, backs Atiku
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Tinubu Northern Youth Forum has announced its decision to withdraw support for President Bola Tinubu and back former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The group also announced a change of identity, adopting the name Arewa Youth For Atiku (AYA) as part of its new political direction. The decision was contained in a statement signed by Adamu Jikan Manu on behalf of the group on November 13, 2026. According to the statement, the formal endorsement of Atiku, declaration of support and official defection to the African Democratic Congress (ADC) will take place on Saturday, November 14, at the party’s North-East Strategic Office in Azare, Bauchi State. The ceremony will be led by the group’s Convener, Hon. Auwal Ibrahim Sansani, CNA. The group said its transition from Tinubu Northern Youth Forum to Arewa Youth For Atiku was intended to provide a broader platform for youth engagement, political awareness, community outreach and participation in the democratic process across Northern Nigeria. It called on its members, supporters, community and religious leaders, youth and women organisations, students, market associations, professionals and other stakeholders to attend the declaration ceremony. The statement said the group believed Nigeria needed responsible leadership, national unity, effective governance and meaningful citizens’ participation. It also urged Nigerians who shared its vision to join its campaign for peaceful and democratic participation ahead of the 2027 general election. The group concluded its statement with the slogan: “Join the Atiku Train. Vote Atiku, Save Nigeria.” The post Tinubu Northern Youth Forum dumps president, backs Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Keyamo: No one sings ‘On Your Mandate’ in place of anthem, accuses NDC of secessionism
item.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has defended the use of the campaign song, On Your Mandate, to welcome President Bola Tinubu at public events, insisting that it is never sung in place of Nigeria’s national anthem. Keyamo also accused the National Democratic Congress (NDC) of promoting secessionism, alleging that singing an outlawed national anthem in place of the legally recognised anthem amounted to an expression of a desire to have a separate country. He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Sunday while responding to what he described as attempts by some individuals to equate the use of Tinubu’s campaign song with the singing of the former national anthem. The minister explained that supporters of Tinubu always observe the national anthem at official events before singing On Your Mandate to celebrate the President. “At no time have supporters of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu sung ON YOUR MANDATE IN PLACE of the National Anthem. At every occasion, the NATIONAL ANTHEM is always sung as a mark of recognition of one of our most important national symbols, and then the President is serenaded by his supporters with ON YOUR MANDATE,” he said. Keyamo maintained that nobody should prevent the presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, from adopting a song, including the former national anthem, as his campaign or personal song. He, however, insisted that such a song must be performed either before or after the legally recognised national anthem has been rendered. The minister also defended the Police Band’s use of the instrumental version of On Your Mandate to herald Tinubu’s arrival at public functions or his decision to address an audience. According to him, the practice is consistent with established presidential protocol, under which the Police Band plays an instrumental piece whenever the President arrives at an event or rises to speak. He cited the administrations of former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo, Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, Goodluck Jonathan and Muhammadu Buhari, saying the Police Band similarly played musical pieces to herald their arrival at the National Assembly or before they addressed gatherings. Keyamo said the On Your Mandate instrumental is sometimes played by the Police Band to announce Tinubu’s presence or speech, but only after the national anthem has been rendered. He further argued that the practice was not unusual, pointing out that several states in Nigeria have their own anthems, which are performed after the national anthem at official functions. The minister, however, drew a distinction between the adoption of a campaign or state anthem and the singing of an outlawed national anthem in place of the officially recognised one. item.title: Abiodun pledges more development for Remoland
item.description: .as Odemo seeks ₦600m for palace reconstruction, highlights security gains, attracts investors to Isara By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the development of Remoland, pledging sustained investments in infrastructure, healthcare, education and economic growth as his tenure gradually winds down. Abiodun also assured the people of Isara-Remo that his administration was working towards establishing a legacy hospital in the community to improve access to quality healthcare and strengthen the delivery of medical services in the area. The governor gave the assurances on Saturday at the 57th Afotamodi Day Festival held in Isara-Remo, Ogun State. The celebration, themed “Preserving Our Heritage, Restoring Our Glory,” also featured a fundraising initiative for the reconstruction of the palace of the Odemo of Isara-Remo, Oba Peter Oluwole Ogunbayo, with an estimated target of N600 million. Speaking through the State Commissioner for Environment, Mr Ola Oresanya, Abiodun described the annual festival as more than a cultural gathering, noting that its 57-year history had established it as an enduring symbol of the identity, traditions and collective aspirations of the Isara people. “For 57 years, this festival has remained a powerful symbol of the history, values, traditions and collective identity of the Isara people,” he said. The governor noted that the festival had continued to provide a platform for preserving the community’s cultural heritage, strengthening family bonds, promoting religious harmony and fostering unity among residents. He commended the Afotamodi Planning Committee, traditional institutions and other stakeholders for initiating the palace reconstruction project, urging Isara indigenes at home and abroad to support its successful completion. According to him, the palace represents far more than a physical structure, as it embodies the authority of the traditional institution, cultural continuity and the collective dignity of the community. “A palace is not merely a physical structure; it is an enduring symbol of traditional authority, cultural continuity, communal pride and the dignity of the institution it represents,” Abiodun stated. On his administration’s development agenda, the governor assured the people that efforts to bridge infrastructure gaps and improve transportation networks across rural and urban communities would be sustained. He disclosed that plans were being advanced for a legacy hospital in Isara-Remo, describing the proposed facility as a strategic investment in the health and wellbeing of the people. He said the hospital, when completed, would improve access to medical services, create employment opportunities and serve as a lasting social investment in the community. item.title: Sex agreement should be part of marriage contract
item.description: By Olaosebikan Olaniyi Marriage is a contract, and every serious contract should be explicit about its most important terms. Sex is central to marriage. It affects emotional bonding, physical health, fidelity, and long-term satisfaction. Leaving it to assumptions and unspoken expectations is why so many marriages fail. A sex agreement as part of the marriage contract makes sense for three clear reasons. 1. It Creates Clarity and Honesty Most couples never have an honest conversation about their sexual needs, boundaries, frequency, and values before marriage. They assume love will handle it. A formal agreement forces that conversation. It allows both partners to state what they want, what they do not want, and what is non-negotiable. Clarity before marriage prevents resentment after marriage. 2. It Protects Consent and Mutual Respect Marriage does not equal automatic consent. A sex agreement affirms that both partners have ongoing rights over their own bodies. It can define consent, right to say no without punishment, agreement on fidelity, protection, and respect for periods of illness, pregnancy, stress, or trauma. This protects both husband and wife and builds a culture of respect, not entitlement. 3. It Prevents Future Conflict Many divorces and infidelity cases stem from sexual incompatibility and unmet expectations. One partner wants sex daily, the other weekly. One sees pornography or open marriage as acceptable, the other does not. One wants children immediately, the other wants to delay. If these issues were agreed upon in writing as part of the marriage contract, couples would either resolve them early or realize they are not compatible before making a lifelong commitment. Including a sex agreement does not make marriage less romantic. It makes it more mature. We sign agreements for money, property, and children. Why should we ignore the very act that creates children and sustains intimacy? Marriage should include a clear, mutual, and voluntary agreement about sex. It is practical, it is respectful, and it is necessary for a healthy modern marriage. Lack Of Sex Is The Biggest Damage In Marriage Many things can damage a marriage like money problems, bad communication and family interference. But none damages a marriage faster and deeper than lack of sex, it is more easy for a marriage to crash when she’s always tired of handling room affairs or when he’s busy pursuing dreams forgetting the importance of marital satisfaction. item.title: Hidden Curriculum of Leadership: What does the environment teach leaders?
item.description: By Dayo Oyinlola Institutions are ecosystems made up of individual units that live in symbiotic relationships with each other. In these environments, information is processed dynamically and learning occurs both formally and informally. We must consider this reality when discussing leadership development. Leaders learn through written documents and institutional codes of conduct: values, laws, behavioral manuals, KPIs and OKRs that organisations establish to hold leaders accountable. And then there are the experiences nobody formally teaches, but everyone learns. A young executive watches how decisions are made. They notice who gets rewarded and who gets overlooked. They observe what happens when someone challenges authority, misses a target, refuses to compromise or asks an uncomfortable question. Nobody necessarily sits them down to teach these lessons. We often think of leadership development as something that happens through formal training, coaching, mentoring and experience. All of these matters, but leaders are also continuously shaped by the systems, institutions, cultures and circumstances within which they operate. And sometimes, the lessons being taught by the environment are very different from the lesson’s organisations believe they are teaching. Consider an organisation that claims to encourage employees to challenge ideas, yet senior leaders consistently dismiss people who disagree with them. Employees then learn that deference is safer than speaking up. Over time, people respond to what they experience rather than what they are told. The environment teaches what is rewarded. It teaches what is tolerated. It teaches how power works, whose voice matters and whether speaking up is valued or punished. It teaches people what leadership really means when it is exercised, not what the organisation says leadership means. This becomes particularly important in difficult operating environments. But there is another question worth asking: What happens when the environment consistently makes the wrong behaviour easier than the right one? If people repeatedly experience an environment where ethical behaviour is punished and unethical behaviour is rewarded, the environment itself becomes part of their leadership development. This is why integrity cannot survive indefinitely as an individual act of courage. For it to become sustainable, it must become part of the collective environment. For leaders operating in contexts where regulatory uncertainty, infrastructure gaps, talent shortages, limited access to capital and complex stakeholder expectations are part of the reality, this distinction becomes even more important. These realities do not excuse poor leadership. But they shape the choices leaders have to make. item.title: It’s time for results, by Funmi Komolafe
item.description: Beloved, it is mid November already. Some are counting the number of days left for 2026 to roll away; others are counting down towards political events in their country. As a Christian what is the focus of your count down? Yours should be a count down to the physical manifestation of your miracle; it should be a count down to the expiration of a challenge in your life. In other words, the count down to the end of 2026 should be for a Christian the time to celebrate results. The one that would celebrate would not give up. However, as human being, we tend to feel disappointed when we have not been able to attain the goals that we set for ourselves. Beloved, lamentations, wearing mournful looks, depression, suicide attempts, all of these do not produce positive results. These expressions should not be associated with a Christian that has deep faith in God and the ability of God to meet all needs. Philippians 2 vs. 13-16 ( KJV) tells us : “ For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure. Do all things without murmurings and disputings: That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world; Holding forth the word of life; that I may rejoice in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain, neither labored in vain”. This passage simply tells us that when we refuse to allow challenges to weigh us down, the Holy Spirit would be active in us and the result would be joy. The Holy Bible gives us a firm warning about complaints, murmurs and the like in 1st Corinthians 10 vs. 10: “ Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer”. A deeper understanding of this passage is that complaints, murmur delight Satan and his demons. It draws one away from God and draws one closer to the enemy that would eventually, destroy and terminate life. Remember, the words of our Lord Jesus in John 10 vs. 9 & 10: “I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly”. So, Brethren, you need to make a choice between holding on to faith and hope in God, or you allow yourself to be destroyed by thoughts of suicide, frustrations, tears etc. However, we are here to lift up faith at a time like this and not to encourage anyone to give up. Rather, what anyone that wants to see an end to a particular challenge needs to do is intensify prayers, praise the Lord at all times, if possible deny yourself some pleasure by going into fasting. item.title: [VIDEO] Atiku Promises To Resume Oil Exploration In Kolmani, Revive Mabilla Power Project
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has promised to resume oil exploration activities at the Kolmani oil field, which he said were suspended under the present administration. He also pledged to restore electricity subsidies and revive work on the abandoned Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project in the North-East. ﻿ Atiku made these promises during his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State on Saturday. Speaking at the rally, he said, “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue.” On his part, Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign, Mr. Austin Akobundu, criticised what he described as the poor governance and misguided policy decisions of the present administration. “There is hunger in the land, and the man who will eradicate it is Atiku,” he said. In the last general election, Atiku secured a significant number of votes in Bauchi State while contesting on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). item.title: 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno
item.description: Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, saying that he will back any coalition that supports President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Eno stated this while fielding questions during a media chat on Saturday. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the President,” he said. “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am for it.” The governor said that the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom is “good on the ground”. Eno, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC after his defection from the PDP in June 2025, said the two parties had agreed to support Tinubu, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and himself in the 2027 general elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to PDP-APC relationship,” the governor said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the President, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” The Rainbow Coalition is spearheaded by Wike to galvanise support for the re-election bid of President Tinubu in 2027. But the coalition has faced opposition from leaders of the APC. In October, 2026, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma said that the Rainbow Coalition has no presence in the state. Speaking during the distribution of campaign vehicles under the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state, Uzodimma insisted that the APC would secure victory in the 2027 elections through organic votes. The governor maintained that the APC was the only recognised political party in the state and urged supporters to vote for the party’s candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Similarly, Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal told the minister to make his political position clear over his involvement with the coalition, insisting that he cannot simultaneously support the APC and other political parties. “Our message is very, very clear: be on one side, you can’t be on two sides. If you are in APC, please come out and support the APC, not you are supporting APC here, and you are supporting some other political parties somewhere else,” he said during an interview with Channels Television’s Inside Sources on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York in October. item.title: Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The Hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked families affected by the deadly attacks in Anguwan Rukuba , in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State that left many killed and several injured in March 2026, to forgive him for not visiting the communities. ﻿ Tinubu spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally in Jos on Saturday. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport. Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland. But I saw the devastation; I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people. “But since then, that has changed; we are forging together. He, however, assured residents that their communities would be rebuilt for those displaced to return home. Tinubu said too many lives had been lost to attacks in Plateau since 2001. He condoled with families who have lost loved ones to such attacks. Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), called for unity, saying speaking different languages should not lead to divisions. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau. “What we should be getting is prosperity, not havoc, not crisis. Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people up from penury to prosperity. “One thousand forest guards are undergoing training right now. You will feel them; you will see them. You will feel secure in your villages and communities,” he added. The President also said the surveillance cameras had been procured as promised. Tinubu assured the residents that his government his working to ease their suffering. A deadly attack in Anguwan Rukuba, in Jos North Local Government Area of the state in March, 2026, left at least 20 people killed and many others injured. On April 2, Tinubu met with the affected families at the Jos Airport, where he condoled with them and assured them that such an incident would not recur. ﻿ The President was criticised for not visiting the affected communities, but his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga , said that said the visit was affected by a scheduled meeting with the President of Chad.
